title: The psychology of sports fans, with Daniel Wann, PhD

sentences.en: This year, more than 120 million Americans watched the Super Bowl on television, the biggest single network telecast audience in history.
sentences.zh: 今年，超过1.2亿美国人通过电视观看了超级碗，这是历史上单一电视网转播观众人数最多的一次。

sentences.en: OK, some of those viewers might have tuned in to see Taylor Swift, but a lot of them were there for the football.
sentences.zh: 好吧，其中一些观众可能是为了看泰勒·斯威夫特，但很多人确实是为了看球赛。

sentences.en: Almost 40 percent of Americans say that they follow sports somewhat or very closely, according to a 2023 Pew Research Center poll.
sentences.zh: 根据皮尤研究中心2023年的一项民意调查，近40%的美国人表示他们或多或少会密切关注体育赛事。

sentences.en: And about 7 percent of them are superfans who follow sports extremely closely and talk about sports every day.
sentences.zh: 其中约7%是超级粉丝，他们极其关注体育，并且每天都在谈论体育。

sentences.en: You might know some of those superfans or maybe you're one yourself.
sentences.zh: 你可能认识其中的一些超级粉丝，或者你自己就是其中之一。

sentences.en: So whether it's college sports, the NFL, the WNBA or Major League Baseball, what drives sports fans to become so passionately attached to their teams?
sentences.zh: 那么，无论是大学体育、NFL、WNBA还是美国职业棒球大联盟，是什么驱使体育迷对他们的球队产生如此强烈的依恋呢？

sentences.en: Is being a fan good for your mental health, even when your team is losing?
sentences.zh: 即使你的球队在输球，成为一名粉丝对你的心理健康有好处吗？

sentences.en: Why are some people fair weather fans while others love to root for the underdog?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人是“看天吃饭”的粉丝，而另一些人却喜欢支持弱势的一方？

sentences.en: What about aggression among sports fans?
sentences.zh: 体育迷之间的攻击性又是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Why do some fans behave badly?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些粉丝表现得很糟糕？

sentences.en: Can playing in front of a big supportive crowd of fans actually affect a team's performance?
sentences.zh: 在大量支持他们的粉丝面前比赛，真的会影响球队的表现吗？

sentences.en: In other words, is there really a home field advantage?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，真的存在“主场优势”吗？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Dan Wong, a distinguished professor in the Department of Psychology at Murray State University in Murray, Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是丹·王博士，他是肯塔基州默里市默里州立大学心理学系的杰出教授。

sentences.en: He's been studying the psychology of sports fans and spectators since the mid-1980s with a particular interest in fans' psychological connection to their teaMs.
sentences.zh: 自20世纪80年代中期以来，他一直致力于研究体育迷和观众的心理学，尤其对粉丝与球队之间的心理联系感兴趣。

sentences.en: He's the author of more than 200 journal articles and multiple books, including Sport Fans, The Psychology and Social Impact of Fandom.
sentences.zh: 他撰写了200多篇期刊文章和多部著作，包括《体育迷：粉丝心理学与社会影响》。

sentences.en: His work has been covered by major media outlets, including ESPN, Time Magazine, The Washington Post, The New York Times, and Sports Illustrated.
sentences.zh: 他的研究成果已被ESPN、《时代》杂志、《华盛顿邮报》、《纽约时报》和《体育画报》等主流媒体报道。

sentences.en: Dr. Wong is a research fellow in the Sport Marketing Association and has won many awards for his research and teaching.
sentences.zh: 王博士是体育营销协会的研究员，并因其研究和教学工作获得了许多奖项。

sentences.en: Dr. Wong, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 王博士，感谢您今天参加我的节目。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: My pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: So let's start with the big question.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从一个大问题开始。

sentences.en: Why do people become sports fans?
sentences.zh: 人们为什么会成为体育迷？

sentences.en: What drives their intense attachment to a sport or a particular team or even an individual player?
sentences.zh: 是什么驱使他们对某项运动、某支球队甚至某位球员产生强烈的依恋？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's so oftentimes the $2 million question, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，这通常是那个价值两百万美元的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: And anytime you have a $2 million question, you can end up with about 2 million different answers.
sentences.zh: 而且每当你遇到一个价值两百万美元的问题时，你最终可能会得到两百万个不同的答案。

sentences.en: So I think that given the time constraints that we might have, I actually teach an entire course on the sport fan psychology that we spend four months talking about this.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，考虑到我们可能有的时间限制，我实际上开设了一门关于体育迷心理学的完整课程，我们花了四个月的时间来讨论这个问题。

sentences.en: But I think that a pretty straightforward answer would be to say that one thing that we know that Sport Phantom does is it really does help individuals meet basic psychological needs.
sentences.zh: 但我认为一个相当直接的回答是：我们所知道的体育迷行为的一件事是，它确实能帮助个人满足基本的心理需求。

sentences.en: That, sure, you can say that, okay, so-and-so follows sport because, well, it's fun or because maybe it provides an escape from, you know,
sentences.zh: 当然，你可以说，某人关注体育是因为它很有趣，或者因为它提供了一种逃避，你知道的，

sentences.en: the stress of life or the boredom of their life or, you know, maybe in some way they enjoy the aesthetics of it,
sentences.zh: 逃避生活的压力或生活的无聊，或者，你知道，也许在某种程度上他们享受其中的美感，

sentences.en: the beauty and the grace and the artistic nature that come with some sport events.
sentences.zh: 那些体育赛事所带来的美、优雅和艺术性。

sentences.en: But really what we've learned in the past about decade is we've sort of undersold ourselves in terms of the psychology of sport fandom,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，在过去十年左右的时间里，我们所了解到的是，我们在体育迷心理学方面有点低估了自己，

sentences.en: and it really does mean more than what we had previously thought.
sentences.zh: 它确实比我们之前想象的意义更重大。

sentences.en: Some examples that I can come up with pretty quickly here would be, for example, by being a fan of a particular team or a sport or even a player,
sentences.zh: 我可以很快举出一些例子，例如，通过成为某支球队、某项运动甚至某位球员的粉丝，

sentences.en: it gives that individual the opportunity to feel a sense of belongingness.
sentences.zh: 它给了个人一种归属感。

sentences.en: We are very social creatures.
sentences.zh: 我们是非常社会化的生物。

sentences.en: Affiliation is certainly, you know, born in us through evolution.
sentences.zh: 归属感当然是通过进化植根于我们体内的。

sentences.en: And one thing that fandom allows people to do is to get into part of these groups.
sentences.zh: 粉丝文化让人们能够进入这些群体的一部分。

sentences.en: I mean, if you reside in a local community and you follow the local team, it's hard to feel lonely.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你居住在当地社区并关注当地球队，就很难感到孤独。

sentences.en: It's hard to feel isolated, right?
sentences.zh: 很难感到被孤立，对吧？

sentences.en: And it gives you this critical link to others.
sentences.zh: 它为你提供了与他人之间至关重要的联系。

sentences.en: But the flip side is also that we don't want to be cookie cutters.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，我们也不想成为千篇一律的人。

sentences.en: We don't want to be exact replicas of everybody else.
sentences.zh: 我们不想成为其他人的精确复制品。

sentences.en: We'd like to stand out in some way, be unique in some way.
sentences.zh: 我们希望在某种程度上脱颖而出，在某种程度上独一无二。

sentences.en: And sport fandom also provides that.
sentences.zh: 而体育迷文化也提供了这一点。

sentences.en: So it gives us this power to be distinct and unique.
sentences.zh: 所以它赋予了我们变得独特和与众不同的力量。

sentences.en: It's funny that when I talk to sports fans, and given what I do, I do that quite frequently, I'll ask them, so who are your favorite teams?
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当我与体育迷交谈时，鉴于我的工作，我经常这样做，我会问他们，谁是你最喜欢的球队？

sentences.en: And let's say I'm talking to somebody who resides near Boston.
sentences.zh: 假设我正在和一位住在波士顿附近的人交谈。

sentences.en: They'll say, well, I love the Red Sox, and I love the Celtics, and I love the Patriots, and I love Manchester United.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我爱红袜队，我爱凯尔特人队，我爱爱国者队，我还爱曼联队。

sentences.en: You're like, wait, what?
sentences.zh: 你会想，等等，什么？

sentences.en: One of these things is not like the other?
sentences.zh: 这些东西里有一个是不一样的吗？

sentences.en: And it's so interesting because that one team allows them to just feel different from everybody else.
sentences.zh: 这非常有趣，因为那支球队让他们感觉与众不同。

sentences.en: So I would say that the most straightforward answer is that people are fans because it helps them meet these basic psychological needs.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为最直接的回答是，人们成为粉丝是因为它帮助他们满足了这些基本的心理需求。

sentences.en: It's not the only way that they can meet these needs, but things like belongingness and the need for the distinction and the need for structure and the need for meaning in life,
sentences.zh: 这不是他们满足这些需求的唯一途径，但像归属感、对独特性的需求、对结构的需求以及对生活意义的需求，

sentences.en: fandom is well-suited to help meet those types of needs.
sentences.zh: 粉丝文化非常适合满足这些需求。

sentences.en: So what's the research?
sentences.zh: 那么研究结果是什么呢？

sentences.en: How do you study fans and find out technically that they really are benefiting mentally from being fans?
sentences.zh: 你是如何研究粉丝并从技术上发现他们确实从成为粉丝中获得了心理上的益处？

sentences.en: Yeah, we do it so many ways.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们通过很多方式来做。

sentences.en: Like so many lines of research in psychology over the years, you find laboratory methods and you also find field research.
sentences.zh: 就像多年来心理学的许多研究方向一样，你会发现实验室方法，也会发现实地研究。

sentences.en: We've done it in my research program both ways.
sentences.zh: 在我的研究项目中，我们两种方式都用过。

sentences.en: We will, you know, engage the, as they've been referred to before, the prey of the social psychology researcher, your lovely psychology introductory students.
sentences.zh: 我们会，你知道，动用那些之前被称为社会心理学研究人员的“猎物”，也就是你们可爱的心理学入门学生。

sentences.en: But I also really like going out into the field and going to sporting events and talking to them and surveying them.
sentences.zh: 但我也非常喜欢走到实地，去参加体育赛事，与他们交谈并对他们进行调查。

sentences.en: I have a research team that pretty much every year we will pick specific sporting events around the area and we'll go to.
sentences.zh: 我有一个研究团队，几乎每年我们都会挑选该地区特定的体育赛事去参加。

sentences.en: And, you know, we always get with these people before the games because I don't want to interrupt their entertainment value as well.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们总是在比赛前和这些人接触，因为我也不想打扰他们的娱乐价值。

sentences.en: But we'll sit down, we'll pass out questionnaires, talk to them.
sentences.zh: 但我们会坐下来，分发问卷，和他们交谈。

sentences.en: And I like doing that because it's in the moment for them, right?
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这样做，因为这对他们来说是当下的体验，对吧？

sentences.en: So if they're at the sporting event, sport is at that point in time salient to them.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们在体育赛事现场，体育在那个时间点对他们来说就是显著的。

sentences.en: And I do think you get some more authentic responses than if they're sitting in a classroom and, you know, stressed out about the test they're about to take in two hours.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为，比起让他们坐在教室里，为两小时后要参加的考试感到压力，你能得到更真实的回答。

sentences.en: So we will use all types of methods.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会使用各种方法。

sentences.en: We'll go to major sporting events.
sentences.zh: 我们会去大型体育赛事。

sentences.en: We'll go to minor sporting events.
sentences.zh: 我们会去小型体育赛事。

sentences.en: We'll go to youth sporting events.
sentences.zh: 我们会去青少年体育赛事。

sentences.en: Then we'll also, you know, just grab the random psychology student that's in a classroom.
sentences.zh: 然后我们也会，你知道，随便抓一个在教室里的心理学学生。

sentences.en: And does it matter to one's health whether you're a fan of, you know, your kid's little league or a national team?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是你孩子少棒队的粉丝，还是国家队的粉丝，这对一个人的健康有影响吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And what we find is it really does not.
sentences.zh: 我们发现其实并没有区别。

sentences.en: What is critical is the extent to which the person does identify with that team.
sentences.zh: 关键在于个人对该球队的认同程度。

sentences.en: A term that we will often throw out there in sports psych is team identification,
sentences.zh: 我们在运动心理学中经常提到的一个术语是“团队认同”，

sentences.en: which is simply the extent to which the fan feels some type of psychological connection to the team.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是指粉丝对球队产生某种心理联系的程度。

sentences.en: How much is the team an extension of the fan?
sentences.zh: 球队在多大程度上是粉丝的延伸？

sentences.en: How central is that team and being a fan of that team to their own self or social identity?
sentences.zh: 那支球队以及成为该队的粉丝，对他们自己的自我或社会认同有多重要？

sentences.en: And what we found is across multiple studies and multiple levels of competition from youth sports, you know, college sports, high school sports, all the way up to, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在多项研究和多个竞争水平中，从青少年体育、大学体育、高中体育，一直到，你知道，

sentences.en: major professional sports in the Olympics is that the more the fan is identified with a local team,
sentences.zh: 奥运会和大型职业体育赛事，粉丝对当地球队的认同度越高，

sentences.en: the greater that that individual is likely to have a well-rounded sense of psychological health, lower levels of loneliness, lower levels of alienation,
sentences.zh: 该个人就越有可能拥有更全面的心理健康感，孤独感更低，疏离感更低，

sentences.en: a higher sense of self-esteem, less social isolation.
sentences.zh: 自尊感更高，社会孤立感更少。

sentences.en: And a critical point is it's not necessarily the team identification itself that drives this finding.
sentences.zh: 一个关键点是，并不一定是团队认同本身驱动了这一发现。

sentences.en: It's the fact that if you identify with a local team, that identification brings with it a group that you can then belong to.
sentences.zh: 事实是，如果你认同当地球队，这种认同会带来一个你可以归属的群体。

sentences.en: And by then getting this sense of belonging, you're then going to get this sense that, well, you know what, I'm not alone in the world.
sentences.zh: 通过获得这种归属感，你就会产生一种感觉，那就是，你知道吗，我并不是世界上孤独的一个人。

sentences.en: And that's a great thing for our well-being.
sentences.zh: 这对我们的幸福感来说是一件好事。

sentences.en: Again, to go back to Boston, if you're walking around a Boston mall here in the early spring with a Boston Red Sox cap, people are talking to you, right?
sentences.zh: 再次回到波士顿，如果你在初春时节戴着波士顿红袜队的帽子在波士顿的商场里走动，人们会和你交谈，对吧？

sentences.en: You've got all of these friends there at the mall.
sentences.zh: 你在商场里有所有这些朋友。

sentences.en: You don't know where they work, you don't know what their name is, you don't know where they live, but they're saying hi to you.
sentences.zh: 你不知道他们在哪里工作，不知道他们的名字，不知道他们住在哪里，但他们会和你打招呼。

sentences.en: It'd be really hard to feel lonely at that point in time.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，真的很难感到孤独。

sentences.en: And the last point that I'll make is that we know that it's changing now, this sense of gaining psychological health from fandom because of the digital age that we're in.
sentences.zh: 我要说的最后一点是，我们知道现在情况正在发生变化，这种从粉丝文化中获得心理健康的感觉，因为我们处于数字时代。

sentences.en: You know, 15 years ago, to follow a sport team and feel connected to others, you kind of had to live in that environment.
sentences.zh: 你知道，15年前，要关注一支运动队并感到与他人有联系，你必须生活在那个环境中。

sentences.en: You can watch a sporting event now from anywhere on the planet and plug in online and feel as though you're actually watching it with others.
sentences.zh: 你现在可以在地球上的任何地方观看体育赛事，在线接入，感觉就像你真的在和别人一起观看一样。

sentences.en: So we're being forced to change some of our thinking about how fandom impacts well-being because, well,
sentences.zh: 所以我们被迫改变一些关于粉丝文化如何影响幸福感的想法，因为，嗯，

sentences.en: being a fan has changed over the last 15 and 20 years because of the social age.
sentences.zh: 由于社交时代，成为粉丝的方式在过去15到20年里发生了变化。

sentences.en: What if your team is having a bad season?
sentences.zh: 如果你的球队表现不佳怎么办？

sentences.en: If you're a really passionate fan, can a loss or a bad season harm your mental health?
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个非常热情的粉丝，输球或糟糕的赛季会损害你的心理健康吗？

sentences.en: I guess that would depend on how you would define harm your mental health.
sentences.zh: 我想这取决于你如何定义“损害你的心理健康”。

sentences.en: Most certainly, it can make you cranky, upset, aggressive, hostile, violent, in a bad mood, surly.
sentences.zh: 当然，它会让你变得暴躁、心烦、好斗、敌对、暴力、心情不好、脾气古怪。

sentences.en: These are the things that would be words that would describe me over the years following both the Cubs and the Kansas City Royals.
sentences.zh: 这些词汇描述了我多年来关注小熊队和堪萨斯城皇家队时的状态。

sentences.en: So I have a lot of expertise with following bad teaMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我有很多关注糟糕球队的经验。

sentences.en: I've kind of perfected it, as a matter of fact.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我已经把它完善了。

sentences.en: The good news, I say, the bad news would be that, yes, certainly following sports teams, because it is central to the identity of highly identified fans, it is going to matter.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，坏消息是，是的，当然，关注运动队，因为它是高度认同的粉丝身份的核心，它确实会有影响。

sentences.en: If you were to take away the emotional response of being a sports fan, you would take away the point of being a sports fan, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你要剥夺作为体育迷的情感反应，你就剥夺了成为体育迷的意义，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, to be a fan is to be emotional.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，成为粉丝就是要有情感。

sentences.en: The elation from the win, the disappointment in the loss, and every potential emotional range in between those two things.
sentences.zh: 赢球时的欣喜若狂，输球时的失望，以及这两者之间所有潜在的情感范围。

sentences.en: But if a fan feels disappointed at the loss, that's just the natural reaction.
sentences.zh: 但如果粉丝对输球感到失望，那只是自然的反应。

sentences.en: They care about these things.
sentences.zh: 他们在乎这些事情。

sentences.en: And, you know, the problem is they can't do a whole lot about it, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，问题是他们对此无能为力，对吧？

sentences.en: They put their heart and soul into following the team, and they're just this idle spectator going, well, I sure hope things go in my direction today.
sentences.zh: 他们全心全意地关注球队，却只是一个无所事事的旁观者，心想，我真希望今天事情能如我所愿。

sentences.en: It's not exactly like I'm the one shooting the free throw, or I'm the one swinging the bat.
sentences.zh: 这并不完全像是我在投罚球，或者是我在挥棒。

sentences.en: So they have this sort of sense of helplessness that can intensify the frustration when they lose.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有一种无助感，这会加剧输球时的挫败感。

sentences.en: But if that occurs, the beauty of it is that nobody, I think, has perfected coping strategies quite like sports fans have perfected coping strategies.
sentences.zh: 但如果这种情况发生，美妙之处在于，我认为没有人能像体育迷那样完美地掌握应对策略。

sentences.en: People will often ask me, what's the craziest thing about sports fans?
sentences.zh: 人们经常问我，体育迷最疯狂的事情是什么？

sentences.en: I really believe that the craziest thing about sports fans is that there actually are sports fans.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为体育迷最疯狂的事情是，竟然真的有体育迷存在。

sentences.en: This has to be the only domain, the only voluntary activity where half the people know, literally,
sentences.zh: 这一定是唯一的领域，唯一的自愿活动，一半的人在字面上知道，

sentences.en: that they're going to be upset when this thing that they consume voluntarily is over, right?
sentences.zh: 当他们自愿消费的这个东西结束时，他们会感到心烦，对吧？

sentences.en: They know that there's at least a 50-50 chance that when they're done, I'm going to be sad.
sentences.zh: 他们知道至少有50%的机会，当比赛结束时，我会感到难过。

sentences.en: I'm not going to want to go to work tomorrow, on and on and on, and yet they're still coming back.
sentences.zh: 我明天不想去上班，等等等等，然而他们还是会回来。

sentences.en: You would never do that if it was like delivery pizza.
sentences.zh: 如果是外卖披萨，你永远不会那样做。

sentences.en: If like half the time they delivered your pizza late, cold, and the wrong pizza, you would not keep going back, sports fans.
sentences.zh: 如果有一半的时间他们送来的披萨又晚又冷，而且还送错了，你不会一直回去，体育迷们。

sentences.en: We just keep going back, and we keep going back because we cope so well.
sentences.zh: 我们只是不断地回去，我们不断地回去是因为我们应对得太好了。

sentences.en: We can look back on the glory years, and it makes us feel better about the fact that our team is terrible now,
sentences.zh: 我们可以回顾辉煌的岁月，这让我们对球队现在表现糟糕的事实感觉好一些，

sentences.en: or we can look to the future and see the future as being even more exciting than it is now.
sentences.zh: 或者我们可以展望未来，看到未来比现在更令人兴奋。

sentences.en: I mean, after all, my team is the worst team in the NFL.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，毕竟，我的球队是NFL中最差的球队。

sentences.en: Hey, that's good news because that means I have the best pick in the draft upcoming, right?
sentences.zh: 嘿，那是好消息，因为这意味着我在即将到来的选秀中有最好的顺位，对吧？

sentences.en: So we just have this way of convincing ourselves that it's all going to be okay.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只是有这种方式来说服自己，一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: It's not okay now, but it's going to be okay in the future.
sentences.zh: 现在不好，但未来会好起来的。

sentences.en: And that's why fans, they just keep coming back.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么粉丝们会不断回来。

sentences.en: Again, I talk to lots of fans, and they so often tell me after losses, I'm never coming back.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我和很多粉丝交谈过，他们在输球后经常告诉我，我再也不会回来了。

sentences.en: 100% of them have come back.
sentences.zh: 他们100%都回来了。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: What about the impact of betting on sports fans?
sentences.zh: 那么博彩对体育迷有什么影响呢？

sentences.en: Those who bet are invested in a different way.
sentences.zh: 那些下注的人以不同的方式投入其中。

sentences.en: What's going on with them, and when they win or lose, what's happening psychologically?
sentences.zh: 他们身上发生了什么，当他们赢或输时，心理上发生了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting, as I look back on the history of sport, and then, of course, the history of fan that comes with it, it seems like every decade or two,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，当我回顾体育的历史，以及随之而来的粉丝历史时，似乎每隔十年或二十年，

sentences.en: there's a major change in how sport is played out that greatly impacts how fans consume and relate to teams and players and leagues and sports in general.
sentences.zh: 体育运动的进行方式就会发生重大变化，这极大地影响了粉丝消费和与球队、球员、联盟以及体育运动整体相关联的方式。

sentences.en: You can think of when night games started, when sport got on TV, when free agency occurred, and all of a sudden,
sentences.zh: 你可以想到夜间比赛开始的时候，体育节目上电视的时候，自由球员制度出现的时候，突然之间，

sentences.en: my favorite team is somehow now pitching for the rival team that I hate so much.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的球队不知怎么地现在正在为我非常讨厌的竞争对手球队效力。

sentences.en: I think that the new thing that we're looking at now is the fact that what was once an absolute giant no-no, which is betting on professional sports, is now not just available,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们现在正在关注的新事物是，曾经绝对禁止的事情，即职业体育博彩，现在不仅可用，

sentences.en: but embraced by the leagues who, just a few short years ago, thought that this was the worst thing that could possibly happen.
sentences.zh: 而且被那些在几年前还认为这是可能发生的最糟糕事情的联盟所拥抱。

sentences.en: That if individuals start to bet on sports, it's going to change how they're a sports fan, it's going to change how they follow teams, and they realize that, you know what,
sentences.zh: 如果个人开始在体育赛事上投注，这将改变他们作为体育迷的方式，这将改变他们关注球队的方式，他们意识到，你知道吗，

sentences.en: maybe it slightly does change how they follow sport and how they follow teams, but guess what?
sentences.zh: 也许它确实稍微改变了他们关注体育和球队的方式，但你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: They do it more often because they have place to bet, and that's really good news for the sports leagues.
sentences.zh: 他们更频繁地这样做，因为他们有地方下注，这对体育联盟来说真是个好消息。

sentences.en: It's kind of surprising that followed fans and studied for something that it took the leagues that long to come around to realize that, hey, betting fans are, guess what,
sentences.zh: 对于研究了这么久的粉丝来说，联盟花了这么长时间才意识到，嘿，下注的粉丝是，你猜怎么着，这有点令人惊讶。

sentences.en: betting fans, so they're going to consume your product.
sentences.zh: 博彩爱好者，所以他们会消费你们的产品。

sentences.en: We've actually conducted some pretty interesting studies that has looked at how we would expect betting to change fandom.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上做了一些相当有趣的研究，探讨了我们预期博彩会如何改变粉丝群体。

sentences.en: We talked to fans, okay, if and when they legalize sport wagering, how will it change your perspective as a fan?
sentences.zh: 我们采访了粉丝，问他们：如果体育博彩合法化，或者当它合法化时，作为粉丝，你的视角会发生什么改变？

sentences.en: And the bottom line from that research is it's really not going to do much, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这项研究的结论是，它其实不会带来太大的改变。

sentences.en: It's not going to change a lot of individuals.
sentences.zh: 它不会改变太多人。

sentences.en: The people that don't follow sport, that could not care less about sport, they're not going to suddenly start following sport because you can bet.
sentences.zh: 那些不关注体育、对体育一点也不感兴趣的人，不会因为可以下注就突然开始关注体育。

sentences.en: And the people that live for sport, they're not going to stop following sport because they can bet.
sentences.zh: 而那些为体育而活的人，也不会因为可以下注就停止关注体育。

sentences.en: They just might slightly consume some games that they wouldn't otherwise have watched, right?
sentences.zh: 他们可能只是会稍微多看一些原本不会看的比赛，对吧？

sentences.en: It would give them a reason to care about a game that their team is not playing or a rival team is not playing.
sentences.zh: 这会给他们一个理由去关心一场并非他们支持的球队或竞争对手球队参加的比赛。

sentences.en: So what our findings are, basically, it would slightly increase the interest for some fans.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的研究结果基本上是，它会稍微增加一些粉丝的兴趣。

sentences.en: Fans that are lower on the scale of interest but still consider themselves a sport, these are the ones that say, you know what, it might make me a little nervous or too anxious,
sentences.zh: 那些兴趣程度较低但仍认为自己是体育迷的粉丝，他们会说，你知道吗，这可能会让我感到有点紧张或焦虑，

sentences.en: so I might not want to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以我可能不想这么做。

sentences.en: So the moderate fans are like, I don't really need a reason to care in a way that's financially going to damage me.
sentences.zh: 所以中度粉丝会觉得，我真的不需要一个在经济上会损害我的理由去关心比赛。

sentences.en: So, but for your typical, I love my team X fan, it just gives them one more reason to follow.
sentences.zh: 但对于典型的“我爱我的球队”这类粉丝来说，这只是给了他们多一个关注的理由。

sentences.en: What about when fans find out that somebody or even a whole team they revered was cheating, was doing something wrong, was doping like Lance Armstrong, for example?
sentences.zh: 那么，当粉丝发现他们崇拜的某个人甚至整个球队在作弊、做错事，或者像兰斯·阿姆斯特朗那样服用兴奋剂时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: What happens to fans then?
sentences.zh: 那时粉丝会怎么样？

sentences.en: Yeah, it really depends on their level of identification, again, their level of psychological connection to the team.
sentences.zh: 这确实取决于他们的认同程度，也就是他们与球队的心理连接程度。

sentences.en: If they're low in identification or moderate, so, you know, maybe it's a team that they sort of associate with or, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果他们的认同感较低或中等，比如，你知道，可能只是他们稍微关联的球队，或者，你知道，

sentences.en: maybe they sort of follow their progress over the course of a year.
sentences.zh: 可能只是在一年中稍微关注一下他们的进展。

sentences.en: But certainly, it would not be something that they would, you know, highly self-identify as a fan of that team.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，这不会是他们会高度自我认同为该队粉丝的那种情况。

sentences.en: For these individuals, they tend to, you know, put down the team or the player and it's going to decrease their likelihood of wanting to be associated with that team.
sentences.zh: 对于这些人，他们往往会，你知道，贬低球队或球员，这会降低他们想要与该队产生关联的可能性。

sentences.en: The term that we use in social psychology is cutting off reflected failure.
sentences.zh: 我们在社会心理学中使用的术语是“切断反射性失败”。

sentences.en: They will cut off their association, at least psychologically and publicly with that team.
sentences.zh: 他们会切断与该队的联系，至少在心理上和公开场合上是这样。

sentences.en: You know, we really, it's, you often hear people say, we're known by the company we keep.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们真的，你经常听到人们说，我们以所结交的朋友来衡量。

sentences.en: And I always tell my students that that's not the point.
sentences.zh: 我总是告诉我的学生，重点不在这里。

sentences.en: The point isn't that we're known by the company we keep.
sentences.zh: 重点不是我们以所结交的朋友来衡量。

sentences.en: The point is that we know that we are known by the company we keep.
sentences.zh: 重点是我们知道我们是以所结交的朋友来衡量的。

sentences.en: We realize that fact.
sentences.zh: 我们意识到了这个事实。

sentences.en: And so, that knowledge changes our behavior and nobody wants to be associated with someone that has done something negative or illegal or that has, like,
sentences.zh: 所以，这种认知改变了我们的行为，没有人愿意与那些做了负面、非法事情的人产生关联，或者说，

sentences.en: threatened the quality of this identity.
sentences.zh: 威胁到了这种身份认同的质量。

sentences.en: Not nobody, actually, because those that are highly identified, you just have to wonder, you know, studying this for four decades,
sentences.zh: 其实也不是没有人，因为那些高度认同的人，你不得不怀疑，研究这个四十年了，

sentences.en: what do players and teams have to do to finally convince somebody that they are not worthy of their love?
sentences.zh: 球员和球队到底要做什么，才能最终让某人相信他们不值得自己的爱？

sentences.en: You know, it's like, I mean, steroids and DUIs and on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像，我是说，类固醇、酒驾等等等等。

sentences.en: And there's still fan bases that hold on to those individuals.
sentences.zh: 但仍然有粉丝群体坚持支持这些人。

sentences.en: And once again, they do so because they have perfected coping.
sentences.zh: 再一次，他们这样做是因为他们已经完善了应对机制。

sentences.en: They've figured out a way to, you know, externalize the individual's transgression.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了一种方法，你知道，将个人的越轨行为外化。

sentences.en: Well, you know, they're under a lot of pressure.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，他们承受着很大的压力。

sentences.en: They're under a lot of stress.
sentences.zh: 他们承受着很大的压力。

sentences.en: Or, well, everybody does it.
sentences.zh: 或者，嗯，每个人都这么做。

sentences.en: Or they actually weren't guilty.
sentences.zh: 或者他们其实并没有罪。

sentences.en: There was an Olympian a few years ago, several years ago now, that was actually caught doping, performance-enhancing drugs.
sentences.zh: 几年前，现在已经是几年前了，有一位奥运选手实际上被抓到服用兴奋剂，即提高成绩的药物。

sentences.en: And huge fans of this sprinter.
sentences.zh: 而这位短跑运动员有大量的粉丝。

sentences.en: One of the more common explanations they had was that the rival runners, sprinters,
sentences.zh: 他们最常见的解释之一是，竞争对手的跑步者、短跑运动员，

sentences.en: had actually switched out his water bottle and put out a water bottle that had the performance-enhancing drugs in it.
sentences.zh: 实际上换掉了他的水瓶，放了一个装有兴奋剂的水瓶。

sentences.en: And they weren't just, like, making this up.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不是在编造这个故事。

sentences.en: They were literally convinced, right?
sentences.zh: 他们确实是深信不疑，对吧？

sentences.en: So the ability of sports fans to find a way to make it all fit and be okay is what allows them to continue to support these individuals.
sentences.zh: 所以体育迷们能够找到一种方式让这一切变得合理并接受它，这正是让他们能够继续支持这些人的原因。

sentences.en: Now, again, they're not completely foolish.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们也不是完全愚蠢。

sentences.en: And they understand that, you know, when somebody does something, they'll say, they shouldn't have done that.
sentences.zh: 他们明白，你知道，当某人做某事时，他们会说，他不应该那样做。

sentences.en: They really shouldn't have done that.
sentences.zh: 他真的不应该那样做。

sentences.en: That was a horrible thing to do.
sentences.zh: 那是一件可怕的事情。

sentences.en: Then they follow that up with, but I'm a forgiving soul.
sentences.zh: 然后他们接着说，但我是一个宽容的人。

sentences.en: And so it's all okay with me.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说一切都好。

sentences.en: Now, why do some people root for underdogs and other people always want to be on the bandwagon with the winning team?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么有些人支持弱者，而另一些人总是想追随获胜的球队？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's so interesting how when you look at people, they either want to pick the surefire winner or the gross underdog.
sentences.zh: 是的，当你观察人们时，这很有趣，他们要么想选择稳赢的球队，要么想选择极端的弱者。

sentences.en: It's like they don't want to pick the team that's 50-50.
sentences.zh: 就像他们不想选择胜负五五开的球队一样。

sentences.en: And the reason is both of those two, picking the high favorite or the serious underdog, the long shot, both of those two are so psychologically safe.
sentences.zh: 原因在于这两者，选择高热门或严重的弱者、胜算极低的球队，在心理上都是非常安全的。

sentences.en: If you pick a team that is, you know, slated to be like a 95% likelihood to win, that's a safe selection.
sentences.zh: 如果你选择一支被认为有95%获胜可能的球队，那是一个安全的选择。

sentences.en: So is picking the team that's a 5% likelihood to win because should that team lose, and it looks like they're going to, you can very easily say, hey, you know, they had no chance.
sentences.zh: 选择一支只有5%获胜可能的球队也是如此，因为如果那支球队输了，而且看起来他们确实会输，你可以很容易地说，嘿，你知道，他们根本没机会。

sentences.en: Now, the advantage is if you pick the underdog and they lose, you can say that, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，优势在于如果你选择了弱者而他们输了，你可以那样说，对吧？

sentences.en: You can say, well, let's be honest, they never really had a chance.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，好吧，老实说，他们从来就没有机会。

sentences.en: Ah, but if they win, isn't that victory that much sweeter?
sentences.zh: 啊，但如果他们赢了，那胜利不是更甜美吗？

sentences.en: Isn't that victory that much better because it's unexpected?
sentences.zh: 那胜利不是因为出人意料而更棒吗？

sentences.en: So I always say that that's where rooting for the underdog relative to a favored team, rooting for the underdog, that's a win-win.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是说，这就是为什么支持弱者相对于支持热门球队来说，支持弱者是双赢的。

sentences.en: If they lose, hey, it's okay.
sentences.zh: 如果他们输了，嘿，没关系。

sentences.en: We're the lovable losers.
sentences.zh: 我们是可爱的失败者。

sentences.en: We're supposed to.
sentences.zh: 我们本该如此。

sentences.en: It's amazing how people like safe choices, underdogs are safe choices.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢安全的选择真是令人惊奇，弱者就是安全的选择。

sentences.en: What about the effect of fans on teams themselves?
sentences.zh: 那么粉丝对球队本身的影响呢？

sentences.en: I mentioned in the intro, the home field advantage.
sentences.zh: 我在开场白中提到了主场优势。

sentences.en: Is it a real thing?
sentences.zh: 这是真实存在的吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: So there's a few ways that research over the years, over the decades, mostly from social psychology, has examined, do crowds matter, right?
sentences.zh: 所以多年来，几十年来，主要来自社会心理学的研究有几种方式来检验观众是否重要，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, certainly they matter to the bottom line and the pocketbooks of the people that own the teams and leagues, but do they actually matter on the field in terms of performance?
sentences.zh: 我是说，当然，他们对球队和联盟所有者的底线和钱包很重要，但他们在场上的表现方面真的重要吗？

sentences.en: And there's a couple of ways that they do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实有几种影响方式。

sentences.en: Certainly, social facilitation, the fact that being around others can kind of get people to rise to the occasion or maybe choke under pressure, that can have a play in this.
sentences.zh: 当然，社会促进作用，即身处他人之中可以促使人们发挥出更好的水平，或者在压力下表现失常，这在其中起了一定作用。

sentences.en: But I think that from a sports psych perspective, most individuals do want to talk about and think about, is there this home field advantage?
sentences.zh: 但我认为从运动心理学的角度来看，大多数人确实想讨论和思考的是，是否存在这种主场优势？

sentences.en: It is one of the most well-replicated and substantiated findings in the realm of sports psychology, that home teams, they just do win more.
sentences.zh: 这是运动心理学领域中最被反复验证和证实的发现之一，主场球队确实赢球更多。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter the level of competition.
sentences.zh: 竞争水平并不重要。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter the type of sport.
sentences.zh: 运动类型并不重要。

sentences.en: Home teams are going to win more.
sentences.zh: 主场球队赢球更多。

sentences.en: Typically, about 60 to 40, home teams will have an advantage.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，大约是60比40，主场球队会有优势。

sentences.en: And they have, over the decades, put forth several potential explanations for this.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，他们为这种现象提出了几种可能的解释。

sentences.en: One popular one a few decades back was travel and fatigue.
sentences.zh: 几十年前一个流行的解释是旅行和疲劳。

sentences.en: Well, you know, traveling several hours, you know, by plane is probably going to wear them down.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，乘飞机旅行几个小时可能会让他们感到疲惫。

sentences.en: I mean, have you looked at the planes these people travel on?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你看过这些人乘坐的飞机吗？

sentences.en: They're nicer than my house.
sentences.zh: 它们比我的房子还要好。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不知道。

sentences.en: You know, they probably get to the hotel and look around and go, this five-star hotel is a dump compared to the airplane that we were just in.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们可能到了酒店环顾四周，然后说，这个五星级酒店和我们刚才乘坐的飞机比起来简直是个垃圾场。

sentences.en: And so, all these other sort of potential explanations, they might matter a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有这些其他潜在的解释，可能有一点影响。

sentences.en: But what research in the last maybe 10 years has found is that what fans are doing is they're influencing the outcomes of the calls of the officials.
sentences.zh: 但过去10年左右的研究发现，粉丝们所做的是影响裁判的判罚结果。

sentences.en: That the officials are the ones far more than the players that are being influenced by the fans.
sentences.zh: 裁判比球员更容易受到粉丝的影响。

sentences.en: A great example of this, there's lots of research.
sentences.zh: 一个很好的例子，有很多研究。

sentences.en: A great example of this is some researchers found that there's actually a home field advantage in Olympics.
sentences.zh: 一个很好的例子是，一些研究人员发现奥运会中实际上存在主场优势。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: But they don't find it for objective sports like the 100-meter dash.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有在客观运动（如100米短跑）中发现这一点。

sentences.en: They find it for subjective sports like gymnastics and diving, where the judges have such a huge impact on the outcome.
sentences.zh: 他们在主观运动（如体操和跳水）中发现了这一点，因为裁判对结果有巨大的影响。

sentences.en: That's where they find the home field advantage, where the officials really do have the biggest say.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们发现主场优势的地方，裁判确实有最大的发言权。

sentences.en: In football games, some football stadiums will have a track, a running track, like the track meet track around the football stadiuMs.
sentences.zh: 在足球比赛中，一些足球场会有跑道，就像田径赛场那样的跑道围绕着足球场。

sentences.en: Others don't have that.
sentences.zh: 其他的则没有。

sentences.en: But you get a higher home field advantage when that track is not there because the fans are that much closer to the officials and they have that much more of an influence on the officials.
sentences.zh: 但当没有跑道时，你会获得更高的主场优势，因为粉丝离裁判更近，他们对裁判的影响力更大。

sentences.en: So, what we know is, yes, the home field advantage is alive and well and an honest thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们知道的是，是的，主场优势是真实存在且有效的。

sentences.en: And it looks like from the current state of the research that the big impact is not on the players themselves as much as it's on the fans having influence on the decisions that the umpires and the referees are making.
sentences.zh: 从目前的研究现状来看，巨大的影响不在于球员本身，而在于粉丝对裁判所做决策的影响。

sentences.en: Are there common traits among certain types of fans, for instance, do some people become fans because they have low self-esteem and they need some external validation?
sentences.zh: 某些类型的粉丝之间是否有共同特征？例如，有些人成为粉丝是因为他们自尊心低，需要某种外部认可吗？

sentences.en: Or do people with, say, violent tendencies revere boxing and mixed martial arts?
sentences.zh: 或者说，有暴力倾向的人是否崇拜拳击和综合格斗？

sentences.en: We've been looking for the recipe for a sports fan for a long time in sports psychology, and I'm sad to say we have not yet found it.
sentences.zh: 在运动心理学中，我们寻找体育迷的配方已经很久了，我很遗憾地说，我们还没有找到它。

sentences.en: Every time we think we might have found one, somebody else comes along as a sports fan and they're completely different.
sentences.zh: 每次我们以为可能找到了一个，就会出现另一个完全不同的体育迷。

sentences.en: If you go to a stadium that has as few as 150, 200 people in that stadium watching a game,
sentences.zh: 如果你去一个只有150到200人在观看比赛的体育场，

sentences.en: you're going to find every single different personality trait possible among those 150 and 200 people.
sentences.zh: 你会在这150到200人中发现所有可能的人格特质。

sentences.en: Now, does that mean that we haven't found certain characteristics of sports fans in research?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是否意味着我们在研究中没有发现体育迷的某些特征？

sentences.en: I mean, we have, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们发现了，对吧？

sentences.en: So, for example, sports fans tend to slide slightly towards an extroverted crowd.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，体育迷往往稍微偏向外向型人群。

sentences.en: That makes sense because, you know, most sports fans, they will consume in a public scenario.
sentences.zh: 这说得通，因为你知道，大多数体育迷会在公共场合消费体育。

sentences.en: But when you look at how much variance is accounted for, right, how powerful these effects are, it's just minuscule, right?
sentences.zh: 但当你观察所占的方差有多大时，也就是这些影响有多强大时，它只是微不足道的，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, what we really say now is that, sure, maybe individuals who tend towards a preference for stylistic things in life would lean towards, I don't know, diving, gymnastics,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们现在真正说的是，当然，也许在生活中偏好风格化事物的人会倾向于，我不知道，跳水、体操、

sentences.en: figure skating, that maybe that's there.
sentences.zh: 花样滑冰，也许这确实存在。

sentences.en: But it's such a small effect that you're way better off saying every kind of person seems to like every kind of sport out there.
sentences.zh: 但这种影响太小了，以至于说各种各样的人似乎都喜欢各种各样的运动要好得多。

sentences.en: We did some research a few years ago where we thought, you know what, I bet there should be a scenario where fans that are,
sentences.zh: 几年前我们做了一些研究，当时我们想，你知道吗，我打赌应该有一种情况，粉丝们是因为，

sentences.en: they're really into it because of the family nature of sport,
sentences.zh: 他们是因为体育的家庭性质而真正投入其中，

sentences.en: that they see sport as an opportunity to spend time with their kids and their spouses, we thought those people, they really shouldn't like violent sports, right?
sentences.zh: 他们将体育视为与孩子和配偶共度时光的机会，我们认为这些人真的不应该喜欢暴力运动，对吧？

sentences.en: That doesn't seem like it should fit.
sentences.zh: 这看起来不应该合适。

sentences.en: Nope, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，完全不是。

sentences.en: We absolutely found that they don't care at all, that they're going to take their kids to the track meet, and they're going to take their kids to the bowling alley,
sentences.zh: 我们绝对发现他们根本不在乎，他们会带孩子去参加田径比赛，带孩子去保龄球馆，

sentences.en: and they're going to take them to the professional wrestling match.
sentences.zh: 还会带他们去看职业摔跤比赛。

sentences.en: It literally did not matter to these people.
sentences.zh: 这对这些人来说完全没有区别。

sentences.en: We also thought that, well, maybe instead they would like stylistic sports, you know, and nope, didn't matter.
sentences.zh: 我们还认为，嗯，也许他们会喜欢风格化的运动，你知道，不，没区别。

sentences.en: It just, every kind of person that you can imagine seems like every different kind of sport that is out there.
sentences.zh: 只是，你能想象到的每一种人似乎都喜欢现存的每一种不同的运动。

sentences.en: And when you factor in how many, you know, millions and millions and millions of fans there are in the world, that kind of starts to make some sense.
sentences.zh: 当你考虑到世界上有数以亿计的粉丝时，这开始变得有些道理了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When does fandom cross the line into something unhealthy?
sentences.zh: 粉丝行为何时会越界变成不健康的东西？

sentences.en: I'm assuming that it sometimes does.
sentences.zh: 我假设有时会这样。

sentences.en: Anytime you have individuals that can get as wrapped up into something as some fans can get into sport, you're going to have individuals who cross the line.
sentences.zh: 任何时候，当个人像一些粉丝投入体育那样投入某件事时，你都会遇到越界的人。

sentences.en: I always refer to this as the darker side of sport fandom.
sentences.zh: 我总是称之为体育迷的阴暗面。

sentences.en: I think that it's critical that we talk about this.
sentences.zh: 我认为讨论这一点至关重要。

sentences.en: I think that it's critical that we don't only talk about this.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们不仅要讨论这一点至关重要。

sentences.en: I think that that was one of the, I mean, it was a criticism of psychology, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为这是其中之一，我是说，这是对心理学的批评，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, for so long, we just didn't want to really talk about the good sides of humanity.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，长期以来，我们只是不想真正讨论人性的好的一面。

sentences.en: Positive psychology comes along, you know, three, four decades ago and, you know, kind of lets us know, hey, it's okay to talk about high self-esteem as well as low self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 积极心理学在三、四十年前出现，你知道，让我们知道，嘿，讨论高自尊和低自尊都是可以的。

sentences.en: That's a good thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件好事。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a good thing to talk about what sport fandom does positively, but we also have to be honest and admit that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我是说，讨论体育迷行为的积极方面是一件好事，但我们也必须诚实并承认，你知道，

sentences.en: there are times when sports fans do things that cross the line.
sentences.zh: 有时体育迷会做一些越界的事情。

sentences.en: I think certainly sport fan aggression is the obvious thing at the top of this list, that there are fans that, I mean, they do things that they should not do.
sentences.zh: 我认为体育迷的攻击性无疑是这个清单上最明显的，有些粉丝，我是说，他们做了一些他们不该做的事。

sentences.en: I mean, they hurl things at players, they say things at players, and they get in fights with fans, and it is not a pretty sight when it occurs.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们向球员投掷东西，对球员说些什么，并与粉丝打架，当这种情况发生时，景象并不美好。

sentences.en: It is rare.
sentences.zh: 这很少见。

sentences.en: So, one of the things,
sentences.zh: 所以，其中一件事，

sentences.en: in addition to the fact that sports fandom can have this facilitating effect for some individuals on aggression where they get too wrapped up in the moment at the sporting event,
sentences.zh: 除了体育迷行为对某些个人在攻击性方面具有促进作用，使他们在体育赛事中过于投入之外，

sentences.en: we can also see some of the darker side in terms of their interpersonal relationships and their lack of care about their job.
sentences.zh: 我们还可以看到在人际关系和对工作缺乏关心方面的一些阴暗面。

sentences.en: That we actually have individuals out there that they'll admit that they will consume sport over 100 hours a week.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上有粉丝承认他们每周消费体育超过100小时。

sentences.en: And if you consume something 100 hours a week, that doesn't give a whole lot of time for, I mean, a loved one, your kids, a job, sleep, food.
sentences.zh: 如果你每周花100小时消费某样东西，那留给爱人、孩子、工作、睡眠、食物的时间就不多了。

sentences.en: It doesn't give a whole lot of time for anything.
sentences.zh: 这几乎没有留给任何事情的时间。

sentences.en: And so, I think that, again, we have to admit that these things are there.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为我们必须再次承认，这些问题确实存在。

sentences.en: Very small percentage.
sentences.zh: 比例非常小。

sentences.en: Most individuals, they will say that sport fandom is a positive influence on their relationship.
sentences.zh: 大多数人会说，体育迷身份对他们的关系有积极影响。

sentences.en: About 2% or 3% will say it probably has some type of detrimental effect.
sentences.zh: 大约 2% 或 3% 的人会说，这可能产生某种负面影响。

sentences.en: But again, if you're going to say that one fight in a crowd is too many, I'm going to say that 2% of individuals having their lives negatively impacted by fandom is 2% too many.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，如果你认为人群中发生一次打斗都嫌多，那我会说，有 2% 的人因迷恋体育而生活受到负面影响，这 2% 也太多了。

sentences.en: It shouldn't have that negative effect.
sentences.zh: 它不应该产生这种负面影响。

sentences.en: And so, we need to talk about the darker side as well.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们也需要谈谈阴暗面。

sentences.en: We need to be honest with ourselves and say, okay, can we do things that lower these numbers, that move the needle?
sentences.zh: 我们需要诚实面对自己，问问自己：好吧，我们能做些什么来降低这些数字，带来实质性的改变吗？

sentences.en: Because if 2% have a negative impact for fandom on their interpersonal relationships, that means there's 2% of relationship partners, right?
sentences.zh: 因为如果 2% 的人因体育迷身份而对人际关系产生负面影响，那就意味着有 2% 的伴侣受到了波及，对吧？

sentences.en: 2% of families.
sentences.zh: 2% 的家庭。

sentences.en: If you have one fight in the stands, okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 如果你在看台上看到一次打斗，好吧，没关系。

sentences.en: That's 2% of people, maybe 3% of people, but that's dozens of people around that individual who had their positive experience seriously interrupted.
sentences.zh: 那只是 2% 或 3% 的人，但那个人周围有几十人的积极体验受到了严重干扰。

sentences.en: And they can feel threatened by this.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会因此感到受威胁。

sentences.en: And we know that one incidence like this is enough to make some individuals shy away from coming back.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，发生一次这样的事件就足以让一些人望而却步，不再回来。

sentences.en: It puts a bad taste in their mouth.
sentences.zh: 这让他们心里很不舒服。

sentences.en: And so, just because it's vastly in the minority, that doesn't mean it isn't worthy of our attention and isn't potentially impacting more people in total than you might think.
sentences.zh: 所以，仅仅因为它只是极少数，并不意味着它不值得我们关注，也不意味着它对总人数的影响比你想象的要小。

sentences.en: Is this kind of aggression among fans on the increase?
sentences.zh: 这种球迷间的攻击性行为在增加吗？

sentences.en: Boy, wouldn't we love to know that.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我们多想知道答案啊。

sentences.en: So, I've been giving these interviews for the better part of three and a half decades.
sentences.zh: 我从事这类采访已经有三十五年了。

sentences.en: That is, for certain, the most common question that I get.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是我被问到最多的问题。

sentences.en: And it is awful to answer the most common question that you get for one-third of a century by saying, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 作为一个研究了三分之一世纪的人，回答这个问题时只能说“我们不知道”，这种感觉太糟糕了。

sentences.en: I wish I had an answer, but I just do not want to lie and not reflect the research.
sentences.zh: 我希望能有个答案，但我不想撒谎，也不想背离研究结果。

sentences.en: And in this case, what research?
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，又有什么研究可言呢？

sentences.en: How would we ever know, right?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么可能知道呢，对吧？

sentences.en: So, when we define aggression among fans, it counts if you're yelling obscenities, as it should.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们定义球迷的攻击性时，如果你在辱骂他人，那就算作攻击，理应如此。

sentences.en: It counts if you're yelling obscenities.
sentences.zh: 如果你在辱骂他人，那就算数。

sentences.en: There's nobody in the stands with a clicker, right?
sentences.zh: 看台上又没人拿着计数器，对吧？

sentences.en: Counting obscenities.
sentences.zh: 专门统计辱骂次数。

sentences.en: Probably there should be, right?
sentences.zh: 或许应该有人统计，对吧？

sentences.en: Maybe we don't want to know those numbers.
sentences.zh: 也许我们并不想知道那些数字。

sentences.en: But I can say this.
sentences.zh: 但我可以这么说。

sentences.en: There are certainly a lot of theoretical perspectives out there that would suggest that, yes, sport fan aggression is on the rise.
sentences.zh: 确实有很多理论观点表明，是的，体育迷的攻击性正在上升。

sentences.en: We might not have absolute concrete numbers.
sentences.zh: 我们可能没有绝对具体的数字。

sentences.en: But we know things that would suggest that it should be.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道一些迹象，表明它应该是在上升的。

sentences.en: For example, we know that team identification can play a role in aggression.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们知道团队认同感在攻击性中起着一定作用。

sentences.en: And we know that people are now more likely to identify with sports teams than there were maybe 20, 40, 60 years ago.
sentences.zh: 而且我们知道，现在的人比 20、40、60 年前的人更容易认同体育团队。

sentences.en: Because other social institutions with which they used to identify work, extended family living close to home, attending religious institutions, these things can be on the decline.
sentences.zh: 因为他们过去认同的其他社会机构——比如住在附近的大家庭、参加宗教活动——这些东西可能正在衰落。

sentences.en: Something has to take the place of that, right?
sentences.zh: 总得有什么东西来取代它们，对吧？

sentences.en: We're not going to stop being, you know, social creatures.
sentences.zh: 我们不会停止成为社会性动物的。

sentences.en: If fandom is chosen as the option to take the place of that, all of a sudden you care more about fandom, all of a sudden you're more likely to get upset if they lose.
sentences.zh: 如果体育迷身份被选为替代品，那么突然之间你就会更关心体育，突然之间如果球队输了，你就更容易感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Society, we're not as nice as we used to be.
sentences.zh: 社会，我们不像过去那么友好了。

sentences.en: You know, empathy levels are going down.
sentences.zh: 你知道，同理心水平正在下降。

sentences.en: Civility levels going down.
sentences.zh: 文明程度也在下降。

sentences.en: People have traced this for many decades.
sentences.zh: 人们已经追踪这个现象几十年了。

sentences.en: If society has less civility, why would we expect there to be anything different among the fans in stadiums, right?
sentences.zh: 如果社会文明程度降低，我们又怎能指望体育场里的球迷会有所不同呢，对吧？

sentences.en: So I can't say, yes, in 2019 the number was this and in 2014 it was this.
sentences.zh: 所以我不能说，是的，2019 年数字是多少，2014 年又是多少。

sentences.en: But I can tell you theories matter.
sentences.zh: 但我可以告诉你，理论很重要。

sentences.en: And we know that there are several theories that would suggest that, yeah, it's on the rise.
sentences.zh: 我们知道有几种理论表明，是的，它正在上升。

sentences.en: And then you can also just say, go to a sporting event, trying to remember what it was like, you know, 25, 45, 55 years ago.
sentences.zh: 你也可以试着去参加一场体育赛事，试着回忆一下 25、45、55 年前是什么样子。

sentences.en: It doesn't feel the same.
sentences.zh: 感觉完全不同了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: 55 years ago, they didn't have family sections.
sentences.zh: 55 年前，他们还没有家庭专区。

sentences.en: They have to have family sections now because they have to, like, quarantine the people who don't want to be exposed to all the rowdy and dysfunctional fans.
sentences.zh: 现在他们必须设立家庭专区，因为他们得把那些不想接触吵闹和失控球迷的人“隔离”起来。

sentences.en: That should tell you that, yeah, maybe something not so pleasant is going on.
sentences.zh: 这应该能告诉你，是的，可能确实发生了一些不太愉快的事情。

sentences.en: Sure, sure.
sentences.zh: 当然，当然。

sentences.en: And the men were wearing suits and the women were wearing dresses.
sentences.zh: 那时候男人们穿着西装，女人们穿着裙子。

sentences.en: Different world.
sentences.zh: 完全不同的世界。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Now, I've read, speaking of age, I've read some reporting that younger people are less likely to be sports fans now than older generations.
sentences.zh: 说到年龄，我读过一些报道，说现在的年轻人比老一辈人更不容易成为体育迷。

sentences.en: There was a recent article in USA Today that was called Gen Z Doesn't Care About Sports.
sentences.zh: 《今日美国》最近有一篇文章，标题是《Z 世代不关心体育》。

sentences.en: Does that track with your experience and research?
sentences.zh: 这符合你的经验和研究吗？

sentences.en: And if it does, what do you think is causing this?
sentences.zh: 如果符合，你认为是什么原因造成的？

sentences.en: There's no doubt that that's true.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，这是事实。

sentences.en: As a matter of fact, one of the recent conversations I had with some of the administration in our university's athletic department was that, you know,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我最近和我们大学体育部门的一些管理人员交谈时，他们提到，你知道，

sentences.en: we draw pretty well for our men's basketball team.
sentences.zh: 我们的男子篮球队上座率还不错。

sentences.en: And Murray State historically has had a pretty good men's basketball team.
sentences.zh: 默里州立大学历史上一直有一支相当不错的男篮队。

sentences.en: And, you know, we'll get, you know, five, six, seven thousand fans for a typical game.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一场典型的比赛我们会有五、六、七千名球迷。

sentences.en: Not bad for a mid-major university.
sentences.zh: 对于一所中等规模的大学来说还不错。

sentences.en: And I, you know, I told our athletic director, I said, if I were you, I'd be nervous because when you look around, you know, they're all in their 40s and 50s and 60s.
sentences.zh: 我告诉我们的体育主管，我说，如果我是你，我会感到紧张，因为环顾四周，你知道，他们大多是 40 多岁、50 多岁和 60 多岁的人。

sentences.en: You don't see very, very, very, very few in their 20s at these sporting events and certainly, you know, not in their teens.
sentences.zh: 你几乎看不到 20 多岁的人出现在这些体育赛事中，更不用说十几岁的青少年了。

sentences.en: There are so many things that individuals that are 15, 20, 25, that they had an opportunity to do and get exposed to when they were growing up that older generations did not.
sentences.zh: 现在的 15、20、25 岁的人，他们在成长过程中有太多机会去接触各种事物，而老一辈人却没有。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There are just more entertainment options that are out there.
sentences.zh: 现在的娱乐选择确实更多了。

sentences.en: When I grew up, you had ABC, CBS, NBC, and pretty much that was it.
sentences.zh: 我成长的时候，只有 ABC、CBS、NBC，基本上就这些。

sentences.en: On a good day, maybe PBS would come in, but that was about it.
sentences.zh: 运气好的话，也许能收到 PBS，但也就这样了。

sentences.en: And and so now how many different options just on TV and streaming and on and on?
sentences.zh: 所以现在，光是电视和流媒体就有多少种不同的选择？

sentences.en: There are the there's such a competition for the entertainment time for the younger generations that we didn't have.
sentences.zh: 年轻一代在娱乐时间上的竞争非常激烈，这是我们当时没有的。

sentences.en: So less likely to be socialized into sport fandom because they're more likely to be doing other things.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不太可能被社会化为体育迷，因为他们更有可能去做其他事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's no doubt that this is true.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，这是真的。

sentences.en: Sport fandom is going to be very interesting in about 30 years when the people that buy tickets are no longer around to buy the tickets.
sentences.zh: 大约 30 年后，当买票的人不再存在时，体育迷文化将会变得非常有趣。

sentences.en: I doubt I'll be here to see that if I am.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑我能不能活到那时候看到这一幕，如果能的话。

sentences.en: I'm really curious how that plays out because it's just fandom is aging out.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇这会如何发展，因为体育迷群体正在老龄化。

sentences.en: But fandom is aging out.
sentences.zh: 体育迷群体确实在老龄化。

sentences.en: And and I'm not saying that there aren't young individuals who are fans.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说没有年轻的体育迷。

sentences.en: There are.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: But just look at a stadium.
sentences.zh: 但看看体育场就知道了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's it's an older crowd relative to what it used to be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，相对于过去，现在的观众群体更老了。

sentences.en: And younger individuals, they have more opportunities.
sentences.zh: 年轻人有更多的机会。

sentences.en: They have more things to do.
sentences.zh: 他们有更多的事情可以做。

sentences.en: And so they're less likely to care about any one thing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不太可能对任何单一事物投入太多关注。

sentences.en: So is this trend having an impact on your course enrollment?
sentences.zh: 那么这种趋势对你的课程注册人数有影响吗？

sentences.en: It does not, thankfully, because there's always enough fans that are out there.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，没有，因为总有足够的球迷存在。

sentences.en: Interestingly enough, I have about 20 percent of my sport fan psychology class that are absolutely not sports fans, that they detest sport.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我的体育迷心理学课上大约有 20% 的学生根本不是体育迷，他们甚至厌恶体育。

sentences.en: They've never followed it and they don't understand it.
sentences.zh: 他们从不关注体育，也不理解它。

sentences.en: And so they take the class to try and figure out what in the world is going on with all these people that are putting all this time and money, you know, into these activities.
sentences.zh: 所以他们选这门课是为了弄清楚，到底是什么让这些人投入这么多时间和金钱在这些活动上。

sentences.en: And it's funny because they'll be apologetic about taking the class.
sentences.zh: 很有趣，他们选这门课时还会感到抱歉。

sentences.en: And I tell them, no, I can't have enough of you people in this class because you give you give the counterbalance to class discussions.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他们，不，我希望班上有更多像你们这样的人，因为你们为课堂讨论提供了平衡。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If it's just all a bunch of sports fans, the class discussion becomes preaching to the choir.
sentences.zh: 如果全是一群体育迷，课堂讨论就变成了“向唱诗班传教”。

sentences.en: The fact that I have three or four or five non fans in there, it sort of serves as a check and a balance to the other individuals.
sentences.zh: 班上有三四个非球迷，这在某种程度上对其他人起到了制衡作用。

sentences.en: And it really makes them do some type of, you know, self-awareness test of, yeah, why why do I do so much of this?
sentences.zh: 这确实让他们进行了一些自我意识测试：是的，为什么我在这上面投入这么多？

sentences.en: Apparently, not everybody does.
sentences.zh: 显然，并不是每个人都这样。

sentences.en: And it gets for much better conversations.
sentences.zh: 这让对话变得好多了。

sentences.en: So in the past few years, a lot of athletes have become more open about their mental health struggles.
sentences.zh: 过去几年，很多运动员开始更公开地谈论他们的心理健康问题。

sentences.en: Do you think that this trend is changing the way that fans relate to athletes and the way that they think about sports in general?
sentences.zh: 你认为这种趋势是否正在改变球迷与运动员的关系，以及他们对体育的整体看法？

sentences.en: You know, as a as a social scientist, I certainly hope so.
sentences.zh: 作为一名社会科学家，我当然希望如此。

sentences.en: I think that sports fans, you know, they're certainly slow to come around.
sentences.zh: 我认为体育迷们，你知道，他们接受新事物的速度确实很慢。

sentences.en: I mean, let's just that just be honeSt. Right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，让我们诚实一点。没错。

sentences.en: I mean, you change a team's logo, just the logo.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你改个球队标志，仅仅是标志。

sentences.en: And for like 20 years, they can't get over what a distrustful and awful scenario that was.
sentences.zh: 他们能为此纠结 20 年，觉得那是一个多么令人不信任和糟糕的局面。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's just the picture of some creature.
sentences.zh: 那不过是一个生物的图片而已。

sentences.en: And for years, we know that athletes were taught to, you know, suck it up.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我们知道运动员被教导要“忍着”。

sentences.en: Don't cry.
sentences.zh: 别哭。

sentences.en: This and that.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: I hope that athletes, by coming out, are changing how fans view athletes and that they're not animals, that they're not robots, that they're actually humans,
sentences.zh: 我希望运动员通过公开这些问题，能改变球迷看待运动员的方式，让他们意识到运动员不是动物，不是机器人，他们实际上是人类，

sentences.en: that they have feelings, that they are fallible.
sentences.zh: 他们有感情，他们也会犯错。

sentences.en: And that what they're doing, their performance is in the public eye.
sentences.zh: 而且他们所做的一切，他们的表现都在公众的注视下。

sentences.en: Everybody gets to see when they have a bad day.
sentences.zh: 每个人都能看到他们表现糟糕的时候。

sentences.en: And I think that a lot of fans would be really upset if everybody and by everybody, I mean, literally millions of people get to see when you messed up at work.
sentences.zh: 我想，如果每个人——我指的是字面意义上的数百万人——都能看到你在工作中搞砸了，很多球迷也会感到非常不安。

sentences.en: I think that that might change their perspective.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能会改变他们的视角。

sentences.en: My hope is that individuals see the humanity in athletics and that we start to give these people a little bit of slack that, you know what?
sentences.zh: 我希望人们能看到运动员人性的一面，我们开始给这些人一点宽容，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It's okay for them to be human, too.
sentences.zh: 他们也是人，这没关系。

sentences.en: I mean, it should be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，本该如此。

sentences.en: They are human.
sentences.zh: 他们是人类。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Like Simone Biles getting the twisties.
sentences.zh: 就像西蒙·拜尔斯（Simone Biles）出现“空中失感”那样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: As it comes out more and fans get more used to it, more athletes will then feel empowered to come out and it will seem less abnormal.
sentences.zh: 随着这种情况越来越多地被曝光，球迷们也越来越习惯，更多的运动员会感到有底气站出来，这看起来就不会那么反常了。

sentences.en: And then that's that snowball that you hope you see over the next 8, 10, 12 years.
sentences.zh: 这就是你希望在未来 8、10、12 年里看到的滚雪球效应。

sentences.en: So what's next for you?
sentences.zh: 那么你接下来的计划是什么？

sentences.en: What else are you looking at?
sentences.zh: 你还在研究什么？

sentences.en: What are the big questions?
sentences.zh: 有哪些重大课题？

sentences.en: So what we've been looking at now actually is fans' beliefs about how they think they can influence the outcomes of sporting events.
sentences.zh: 我们现在研究的其实是球迷关于他们认为自己如何能影响体育赛事结果的信念。

sentences.en: We know that they sort of can by, you know, maybe potentially have an impact on the players, but definitely having an impact on officials.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们确实能通过某种方式，比如潜在地影响球员，但肯定能影响裁判。

sentences.en: We've been asking them, what do you do to try and influence the outcome?
sentences.zh: 我们一直在问他们，你做了什么来试图影响结果？

sentences.en: So to what extent do you have superstitions, prayer, yell encouragement, yell derogatory comments towards the officials and the other team?
sentences.zh: 那么你在多大程度上会有迷信行为、祈祷、大声鼓励，或者对裁判和对方球队大喊侮辱性言论？

sentences.en: And what we found was so interesting in the first study that's under review at a journal now is that all of the different methods that they use are positively correlated.
sentences.zh: 我们在第一项研究中发现了一个非常有趣的结果，该研究目前正在期刊审稿中，即他们使用的所有不同方法之间都呈正相关。

sentences.en: So the more they use one method, the more they use another.
sentences.zh: 所以他们使用一种方法越多，使用另一种方法也就越多。

sentences.en: That to me is absolutely hysterical because it means that the more someone is likely to cuss out an official to help the team win, is also more likely to pray to help the team win.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说简直太搞笑了，因为这意味着一个人越可能为了球队获胜而辱骂裁判，也就越可能为了球队获胜而祈祷。

sentences.en: And somewhere, that to me is just so wonderfully funny.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这对我来说真是太有趣了。

sentences.en: I can't get past it.
sentences.zh: 我无法释怀。

sentences.en: The state that we're starting now that will begin this fall is, now that we know that fans engage in these acts to try and influence, we're now asking them,
sentences.zh: 我们现在开始的、将于今年秋季进行的研究是，既然我们知道球迷会采取这些行为来试图施加影响，我们现在问他们，

sentences.en: which ones do you think work best, right?
sentences.zh: 你认为哪种方法最有效，对吧？

sentences.en: We know what they do.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们做了什么。

sentences.en: Now, we'd like to know, okay, so, you know, pitchers have their go-to pitch.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们想知道，好吧，你知道，投手有他们的拿手球。

sentences.en: Point guards have their go-to move.
sentences.zh: 控球后卫有他们的拿手绝活。

sentences.en: We want to know what the fans' go-to active influence is.
sentences.zh: 我们想了解粉丝们在遇到这种情况时的首选应对方式。

sentences.en: When it's really close, right?
sentences.zh: 当比分非常接近的时候，对吧？

sentences.en: When it's really close, do you cuss or do you pray or do you rub your lucky rabbit's foot?
sentences.zh: 当比分非常接近时，你会咒骂、祈祷，还是会摸摸你的幸运兔脚？

sentences.en: That's what we're after now.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们现在想探讨的。

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是个很好的问题。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Wan, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，万博士，感谢您今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: This has been a lot of fun.
sentences.zh: 这次访谈非常愉快。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Absolutely been my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。
